stream notes / expected+observed reference-frame coverage:
  MID-STREAM RESOLUTION CHANGE: frames 0-5 coded at 96x64 (frame 0 forced keyframe,
  1-5 inter LAST-only), frames 6-11 coded at 64x48 (all inter). Produced via a custom
  C program (scaled_encoder.c, in this directory) against libvpx v1.15.2's public API
  -- vpx_codec_enc_config_set() with a new g_w/g_h between frames, the same mechanism
  libvpx's own conformance test test/resize_test.cc uses -- because no vpxenc/ffmpeg
  CLI flag exposes an exact, deterministic, forced-frame-index resolution change (see
  RECIPE.md 'scaled: method that worked' for the flags that do NOT do this).
  kf_mode=VPX_KF_DISABLED so the ONLY keyframe is the one forced at frame 0 (guards
  against an auto-inserted keyframe silently coinciding with/replacing the resize
  point). Expected+observed at coded frame 6 (the first 64x48 frame): frame_type=inter,
  intra_only=0 (i.e. genuinely non-key, non-intra-only despite the size change) --
  the single most important static fact this stream exists to prove. All 3
  found_ref bits are 0 at frame 6 (none of the 3 reference slots -- all still holding
  96x64 pictures -- match the new 64x48 size), forcing an EXPLICIT frame_size() read
  instead of the found_ref shortcut; VP9's built-in reference-scaling motion
  compensation (decoder-side, invoked whenever a used reference's stored dimensions
  differ from the current frame's, independent of how frame_size_with_refs() resolved
  the current size) is what makes ref_frame_idx pointing at 96x64 slots legal for a
  64x48 inter frame at all. IMPORTANT: ffmpeg's forced-libvpx-vp9 rawvideo decode of
  this stream silently re-normalizes every output frame to the FIRST frame's
  dimensions (96x64) -- confirmed via ffmpeg's own log line 'dimension change! 96x64 ->
  64x48' immediately followed by a wrong, constant-96x64-sized rawvideo byte count
  (110592 = 12*9216, i.e. every frame padded/rescaled back to 96x64). scaled.ref.yuv is
  therefore the vpxdec (not ffmpeg) decode for this stream ONLY -- vpxdec is libvpx
  directly, satisfying the 'decoder identity = libvpx' requirement at least as strongly
  as the ffmpeg wrapper, and its per-resolution-pattern output (%wx%h) independently
  confirmed exactly 6 frames at 96x64 then 6 at 64x48, matching this parser's header-
  parsed dims exactly. See the byte-offset table below (and RECIPE.md) for the exact
  heterogeneous layout of scaled.ref.yuv.
  frame_parallel_decoding_mode=0 on every frame (explicit VP9E_SET_FRAME_PARALLEL_DECODING
  control in scaled_encoder.c) -- adapt=YES throughout, incidental to this stream's
  purpose but consistent with p5single/compound.
